freshness.policy: Change-driven: any newer cited source review invalidates the question snapshot. No calendar-based expiry; re-retrieve and independently review after documentation/taxonomy changes. Fresh is relative to checked-in evidence, not a claim of perpetual correctness.

sources.title: Roles and permissions in the Microsoft Sentinel platform
sources.shortSummary: Sentinel Reader views resources, Responder also manages incidents, Contributor edits resources, and Playbook Operator manually runs playbooks. Automation uses a separately authorized service account. Sentinel read roles do not confer Defender workload detection-management permissions.

sources.title: Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel
sources.shortSummary: Playbooks use Logic Apps. User permissions and the Sentinel service account's Automation Contributor permission on the playbook resource group are separate. The cited role behavior does not use the page's Preview playbook templates.

sources.title: Automate threat response in Microsoft Sentinel with automation rules
sources.shortSummary: Automation evaluates the current incident state, runs sequentially, and completes applicable creation-trigger rules before update-trigger rules. Negative tag conditions distinguish individual tags from the collection. Preview Simple Flows are outside the cited claims.

sources.title: Quick threat detection with near-real-time (NRT) analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel
sources.shortSummary: NRT analytics run every minute over ingestion-time windows with a two-minute delay. Single-event grouping produces at most 30 alerts; above 30 results, the final alert summarizes all applicable events.

sources.title: Create custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR
sources.shortSummary: Custom detections require permissions for each targeted service. Recommended event identifiers preserve alert enrichment. Continuous frequency requires one supported table, supported operators, GA columns, no joins/unions/externaldata, and no comments.

sources.title: Syslog and Common Event Format (CEF) via AMA connectors for Microsoft Sentinel
sources.shortSummary: CEF messages are ingested into CommonSecurityLog and plain Syslog into Syslog. Shared facilities can duplicate ingestion; if facilities cannot be changed, filter CEF from the Syslog stream, checking both ProcessName and SyslogMessage for affected AMA versions.

sources.title: Ingest syslog and CEF messages to Microsoft Sentinel with the Azure Monitor Agent
sources.shortSummary: The portal's collection rule selects a minimum severity per facility. Choosing LOG_ERR also collects LOG_CRIT, LOG_ALERT, and LOG_EMERG. Non-Azure forwarders require Azure Arc Connected Machine agent.

sources.title: Take response actions on a device
sources.shortSummary: Manual device isolation, app restriction, evidence collection, and antivirus scans have distinct purposes and prerequisites. Full-tunnel VPNs can block cloud connectivity after isolation. High-value asset configuration can restrict live response. Automatic isolation Preview and the outdated manual-AIR section are excluded.

sources.title: Investigate entities on devices using live response
sources.shortSummary: Live response distinguishes file metadata from file download, records command status, and supports background downloads. Ctrl+C cancels the portal command rather than stopping the agent-side operation. Uploading through a live session requires Manage Security Settings.

sources.title: View and manage actions in the Action center
sources.shortSummary: Pending actions can be approved or rejected; supported completed actions can be undone from History. Bulk undo requires the same action type. The article announces September 1, 2026 retirement of the separate Endpoint AIR experience; Office 365 AIR remains available.

sources.title: DeviceProcessEvents
sources.shortSummary: Process-creation records distinguish the created process from the initiating process. Created-process signing information is obtained through its SHA1 and certificate information, not initiating-process signature or version metadata. ProcessUniqueId is the Windows Process Start Key.

sources.title: DeviceNetworkEvents
sources.shortSummary: Network events contain remote destinations and initiating-process fields. InitiatingProcessSHA256 is usually unpopulated; use available SHA1. InitiatingProcessUniqueId identifies a process instance, while ReportId is a repeating event counter.

sources.title: innerunique join
sources.shortSummary: An unspecified KQL join kind defaults to innerunique, which deduplicates left-side keys before matching. Which duplicate left row survives is not a reliable selection contract.

sources.title: inner join
sources.shortSummary: An explicit inner join produces each matching left/right pair and does not perform the default innerunique left-key deduplication.

sources.title: arg_max() (aggregation function)
sources.shortSummary: Within summarize, arg_max returns the maximizing row and specified columns from that same row. Separate max expressions do not preserve a row association.

sources.title: summarize operator
sources.shortSummary: Summarize produces one row for each combination of grouping values, computing aggregates per group. Time buckets require explicit bin expressions; grouping by raw Timestamp keeps distinct timestamps separate.

sources.title: Threat hunting in Microsoft Sentinel
sources.shortSummary: In Sentinel-specific Hunting, bookmarks preserve selected result rows, the originating query, notes, and tags. Bookmarks are not available in unified Advanced hunting. Preview Hunts and unavailable livestreams are excluded.

sources.title: Restrict response actions on high-value assets
sources.shortSummary: Selective Response Actions can disallow live-response sessions on a supported high-value asset despite broader tenant permissions. Device security-operations information exposes enabled and disabled capabilities. No Preview designation appears for this restriction in the fetched article; an older linked deployment-tool label should be independently assessed.

sources.title: Logical (binary) operators
sources.shortSummary: KQL equality compares operands; and requires both predicates, while or accepts either predicate. A compound hunting filter must use conjunction when both image identity and destination must match.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/sentinel-roles.json confirms the built-in role matrix: Responder = Reader plus manage incidents, without analytics-rule or playbook editing. The task-matrix row for Contributor adds create/edit analytics rules, and Playbook Operator only lists/views/runs playbooks. Answer key b is uniquely defensible.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Role matrix in raw/sentinel-roles.json directly lists Responder as Reader plus incident management with no analytics or playbook editing.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/playbooks.json confirms that Microsoft Sentinel's service account requires Automation Contributor on the resource group where the playbook resides, and raw/sentinel-roles.json confirms the human maintainer's role is unrelated to the execution identity. Answer d fixes exactly the scoped service-account authorization the scenario removed.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/playbooks.json states Sentinel needs Automation Contributor on the resource group where the playbook resides.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/playbooks.json Playbook Operator description ("Lets you run a playbook manually") and Logic App Contributor ("Edit and manage logic apps") supports a as the least-privilege human role. The scenario supplies service-account permissions separately, so Automation Contributor and Reader are excluded.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/playbooks.json describes Playbook Operator as manual playbook run and separates Logic App Contributor and Automation Contributor scopes.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/automation-reference.json Notes on execution order and priority section confirms: each trigger type has its own queue, creation-trigger rules run in full before update-trigger rules, and later rules see the incident state after earlier actions. Answer c is the only outcome consistent with all three rules.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Notes on execution order and priority in raw/automation-reference.json establishes trigger-type queues, creation-before-update sequencing, and current-state evaluation.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/automation-reference.json Tag property: individual vs. collection section confirms that Any individual tag operators evaluate per-tag (so needs-triage would satisfy a per-tag not-contains) while Collection-of-all-tags operators evaluate the set as one unit. Only the collection-level not-contains excludes an incident carrying approved-maintenance.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Tag property: individual vs. collection in raw/automation-reference.json distinguishes per-tag from collection-level negatives with worked examples.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/nrt-rules.json How NRT rules work confirms that Sentinel NRT queries events on their ingestion time (not TimeGenerated) with a two-minute delay and a one-minute cadence, and the Considerations section documents the 12-hour delay ceiling. An eight-minute-old event ingested during the evaluated minute is inside the ingestion window.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/nrt-rules.json documents ingestion-time evaluation, two-minute delay, one-minute cadence, and a 12-hour delay ceiling.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/custom-detections.json shows the recommended pattern uses arg_max(Timestamp, ReportId) inside summarize to retain the same event's identifier alongside a device-level count. Independent maxima and by grouping do not preserve the same-row association; option d drops ReportId entirely. Answer c matches the documented example.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/custom-detections.json example uses arg_max(Timestamp, ReportId) directly, and raw/arg-max.json confirms the maximizing-row column semantics.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/custom-detections.json Tables that support Continuous (NRT) frequency and raw/nrt-rules.json Considerations confirms the two engines are distinct: Defender Continuous requires one supported table, supported operators, GA columns, no joins/unions/externaldata and no comments; Sentinel NRT explicitly allows queries across multiple workspaces and more than one table. P satisfies Continuous; S needs Sentinel NRT.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/custom-detections.json Continuous (NRT) restrictions and raw/nrt-rules.json Considerations independently constrain the two engines' allowed query shapes.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/ama-architecture.json Data ingestion duplication avoidance confirms the constrained alternative when facilities cannot be changed: filter CEF messages from the Syslog ingestion stream via DCR transformation. Starting with AMA 1.41, ProcessName is unreliable for nonstandard headers, so the transform must check both ProcessName and SyslogMessage. Answer a captures the full documented workaround.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/ama-architecture.json documents both the shared-facility duplication and the AMA 1.41 dual-field transform for the Syslog stream.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/ama-overview.json Collect step confirms the portal selects a minimum severity per facility: selecting LOG_ERR collects LOG_ERR, LOG_CRIT, LOG_ALERT, and LOG_EMERG. Answer d matches the documented inclusive minimum semantics.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/ama-overview.json Collect tab section spells out the LOG_ERR minimum-selection inclusion.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/live-response.json basic and advanced command tables confirms fileinfo returns metadata for a file without transferring or modifying it, getfile downloads a file, putfile places a library file on the device, and remediate for a file deletes it. Answer c uniquely satisfies the read-only requirement.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/live-response.json command tables directly define fileinfo, getfile, putfile, and remediate.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/live-response.json Cancel a command note confirms Ctrl+C cancels the command in the Microsoft Defender portal but does not stop the agent-side operation; changing operations such as remediate may continue. The Command log records command details and status, so responders must inspect actual outcome rather than infer rollback from the UI. Answer a matches this documented warning.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/live-response.json Cancel a command note explicitly warns Ctrl+C is a portal cancellation and does not stop the agent-side operation.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/live-response.json Other requirements section confirms uploading through a live-response session console requires the Manage Security Settings permission and that the button is greyed out for users with only delegated permissions; separate Library management upload does not require this permission. Answer d is the documented explanation.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/live-response.json Other requirements explains the Manage Security Settings dependency for the session upload button and the separate Library management route.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/remediation-actions.json Review pending actions confirms Approve initiates a selected pending action, Reject prevents it, and Go hunt opens Advanced hunting. Undo lives on History. The current retirement notice explicitly excludes Defender for Office 365 AIR from the change, so Approve on Pending remains the documented Office 365 workflow. Answer b is uniquely correct.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/remediation-actions.json Review pending actions section defines Approve and the retirement note preserves Office 365 AIR.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/network-events.json and raw/process-events.json confirms DeviceNetworkEvents carries RemoteIP, RemotePort, and initiating-process fields for connection events, while DeviceProcessEvents is a process-creation table without those network-destination columns. Answer a is the documented table.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/network-events.json defines RemoteIP, RemotePort, and initiating-process fields for connection rows; raw/process-events.json describes DeviceProcessEvents as a creation table.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/process-events.json confirms InitiatingProcess signature and signer fields describe the initiating process, and ProcessVersionInfo* is file metadata that does not indicate signing status. The documented technique for created-process signing information is joining its SHA1 to DeviceFileCertificateInfo. Answer d matches the documented join key.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/process-events.json note explicitly tells hunters to join created-process SHA1 to DeviceFileCertificateInfo and disqualifies initiating-process signature fields and version metadata.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/process-events.json and raw/network-events.json confirms ProcessUniqueId and InitiatingProcessUniqueId both equal the Windows Process Start Key, while ReportId is a repeating event counter. Correlating a network event to the exact launch requires network.InitiatingProcessUniqueId (the network actor) to process.ProcessUniqueId (the newly created process record), retaining DeviceId to survive multi-device data. Answer c is the only pairing that avoids parent/reused-PID/event-counter confusion.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/process-events.json and raw/network-events.json equate ProcessUniqueId and InitiatingProcessUniqueId with the Windows Process Start Key; ReportId is described as repeating.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/innerunique.json confirms the default join kind deduplicates left-side keys, and raw/inner.json confirms explicit inner emits every matching left/right pair. Right-side uniqueness does not disable left-side deduplication, so kind=inner uniquely preserves all three matching connection rows. Difficulty downgraded to advanced because the reasoning centers on one documented default behavior rather than multi-step architecture.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/innerunique.json states the default flavor deduplicates left keys, and raw/inner.json describes inner as producing every matching left/right pair.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/summarize.json confirms summarize creates one output row per combination of by-expressions and that time buckets require explicit bin() expressions. Grouping by DeviceId and bin(Timestamp, 15m) produces the documented per-device, per-15-minute-interval result; the other options either drop DeviceId, drop the time grouping, or keep the raw Timestamp.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/summarize.json documents grouping expressions and explicit bin() datetime buckets in the Notes.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent read of raw/sentinel-hunting.json confirms that bookmarks in the Sentinel-specific Hunting experience preserve selected result rows, the originating query, notes, and tags, and that bookmarks are not available in unified Advanced hunting. Favoriting a query only reruns it. Answer b is the documented mid-investigation action.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: raw/sentinel-hunting.json describes bookmarks preserving selected rows, query, notes, and tags, and marks unified Advanced hunting as lacking bookmarks.
